title.en: Act III: Banquo and the banquet

heading.en: A crown that brings no peace

hook.en: Macbeth is king, yet he cannot rest. The Witches promised the crown to Banquo's children; so Banquo must die. And then a ghost comes to dinner.

narration.en: Macbeth is king, yet he cannot rest. The Witches promised the crown to Banquo's children; so Banquo must die. And then a ghost comes to dinner.

body.en: Banquo suspects that Macbeth played foully to become king, yet hopes the prophecy for his own descendants will also come true. Macbeth, now king, feels his crown is fruitless: he has no heir, and Banquo's children are promised the throne. He hires murderers, persuading them that Banquo is their enemy, and does not tell his wife of the plan. Banquo is killed on his way to the feast, but his son Fleance escapes, so the threat to Macbeth's line remains.

points.en: He hires murderers without telling his wife

text.en: Unease
Banquo suspects; Macbeth feels his
crown is fruitless without heirs.
The plot
Macbeth persuades two murderers
and keeps his wife in the dark.
Half-success
Banquo is killed, but Fleance
escapes in the dark.
Climax
At the feast only Macbeth sees the ghost;
his guests see him rave.
Aftermath
The feast breaks up; Macbeth resolves to
visit the Witches; Scotland grows suspicious.

body.en: At the feast for the lords, Macbeth hears from a murderer that Fleance has escaped. When he toasts the absent Banquo, the ghost appears in Macbeth's seat, seen by him alone. His terrified outbursts alarm the guests; Lady Macbeth tries to cover for him, saying he has had fits since youth, and then sends the guests away. Macbeth notes that Macduff stayed away and decides to visit the Witches; he feels he has waded so deep in blood that going back is as hard as going on. The scene shows public guilt breaking through and the Macbeths drifting apart.

points.en: The ghost is seen only by Macbeth
Lady Macbeth covers for him and dismisses the guests
Macbeth will go on in blood

explanation.en: Macbeth now acts on his own and is haunted; Lady Macbeth is uneasy and covering up; Banquo pays for his knowledge.

problem.en: Why does Macbeth want Banquo dead? Give three reasons.

steps.en: Banquo knows of the prophecies and may suspect Macbeth of murdering Duncan.
The Witches promised that Banquo's descendants would be kings, so Macbeth's crown would pass to them, not to his own heirs.
Macbeth fears Banquo's courage and wisdom, which make him a natural rival and threat.

answer.en: Fear of exposure, of Banquo's royal line, and of Banquo himself.
